questions.question: What is the aim of viral RNA/DNA extraction?

explanations.a: Growing viruses requires host cells and cell culture media, not extraction.
explanations.c: Extraction isolates nucleic acids and does not focus on disinfection/killing.
explanations.d: Staining is done for visualization under microscopes, not extraction.

questions.question: Viral RNA/DNA is enclosed within which structure?

explanations.a: Ribosomes are cell organelles responsible for translation, not encapsulation.
explanations.b: Viruses do not possess cell walls.
explanations.d: Viral genetic material is enclosed in a capsid rather than a cellular nucleus.

questions.question: Which sample can be used for viral nucleic acid extraction?

explanations.a: Serum contains viral particles and can be used.
explanations.b: Plasma contains viral particles and can be used.
explanations.c: Supernatant from viral cultures contains released viral particles and can be used.

questions.question: Which downstream application requires extracted viral RNA?

explanations.a: Western blot is used for protein detection.
explanations.c: ELISA detects antigen or antibody proteins.
explanations.d: SDS-PAGE is used to separate proteins by molecular weight.

questions.question: Which precaution is most important during RNA extraction?

explanations.a: RNA is highly sensitive to heat and degrades easily at high temperatures.
explanations.c: Tube color does not affect RNA stability.
explanations.d: Vortexing excessively can shear genomic DNA but doesn't prevent RNA degradation specifically.

questions.question: Why should RNA samples be stored at −80 °C?

explanations.a: Freezing does not alter the concentration of the solute.
explanations.c: Storage temperature does not affect sample purity.
explanations.d: Binding steps are performed during extraction, not storage.

questions.question: What is the main difference between RNA and DNA?

answers.c: RNA contains uracil instead of thymine

explanations.a: RNA contains uracil instead of thymine.
explanations.c: RNA contains uracil instead of thymine.
explanations.d: They differ in their sugars (ribose vs deoxyribose) and nitrogenous bases.

questions.question: Which enzyme is used to convert RNA into complementary DNA (cDNA)?

explanations.c: RNase degrades RNA rather than converting it.

questions.question: Which condition can lead to degradation of RNA during handling?

explanations.b: Wearing gloves protects the sample from skin RNases.
explanations.d: Keeping samples on ice slows down enzymatic degradation.
